questions.question: What tragic industrial accident took place at Bhopal in 1984?

options.B: Deadly gas escape from a chemical plant

questions.explanation: The text mentions a 'tragic industrial accident' at Bhopal where 'deadly gas' escaped into the atmosphere.

questions.question: On which date did the Bhopal Gas Tragedy occur?
questions.explanation: The industrial accident occurred at Bhopal on 3 December, 1984.

questions.question: Which company operated the chemical plant in Bhopal in 1984?
questions.explanation: The gas escaped from a chemical plant operated by Union Carbide.

questions.question: How many local residents were killed by the gas leak in Bhopal?
questions.explanation: The leak killed over 4000 local residents.

questions.question: What happened to a large section of the surviving population in Bhopal?

options.B: They were rendered blind and crippled.

questions.explanation: The gas leak rendered blind and crippled a large section of the surviving population.

questions.question: How long can a man typically live without food?
questions.explanation: The text states, 'A man can live without food for a month'.

questions.question: How long can a man live without water?
questions.explanation: A man can live without water for 'two or three days'.

questions.question: How long can a man live without breathing?
questions.explanation: The text states he 'cannot live without breathing even for a minute'.

questions.question: An average adult exchanges how much air per day?
questions.explanation: It is estimated that an average adult exchanges 15 kg of air a day.

questions.question: Which gaseous element makes up 78 percent of dry air?
questions.explanation: Air comprises 78 percent nitrogen.

questions.question: What is the percentage of oxygen in dry air?
questions.explanation: Air comprises 21 percent oxygen.

questions.question: What is the percentage of carbon dioxide in the air?
questions.explanation: Air contains 0.03 percent carbon dioxide.

questions.question: Together with argon, the main gases make up what percentage of dry air?
questions.explanation: These elements make up 99.9 percent of dry air.

questions.question: Inhalation of polluted air can lead to what kind of disorders?
questions.explanation: Inhalation of this polluted air can lead to respiratory disorders.

questions.question: Our air is being poisoned with by-products from what kind of society?
questions.explanation: Our air is being poisoned with the by-products of an expanding technological society.

questions.question: What do most industries spew from their chimneys?
questions.explanation: Most of these industries spew dense smoke from their chimneys.

questions.question: Which of these fuels is NOT mentioned as being burnt by industries to produce steam?
questions.explanation: The text mentions coal, coke, and furnace oil.

questions.question: Industrial smoke contains which of the following?

options.B: Obnoxious gases, ash and dust particles

questions.explanation: We respire polluted air containing obnoxious gases, ash and dust particles.

questions.question: Which industries are rated first among those discharging high amounts of smoke and ash?
questions.explanation: Thermal power stations are rated the first among the industries that discharge high amounts of smoke and ash.

questions.question: What do chemical industries release into the air along with smoke?
questions.explanation: Some chemical industries also release toxic fumes into the air.

questions.question: How many tonnes of pollutants do automobiles spew in Greater Kolkata every day?
questions.explanation: Automobiles in Greater Kolkata spew about 1500 tonnes of pollutants daily.

questions.question: A person in Kolkata is forced to inhale toxic substances equivalent to smoking how many cigarette packets a day?
questions.explanation: A person in Kolkata is forced to inhale toxic substances equivalent to smoking two packets of cigarettes a day.

questions.question: Automobiles are responsible for what percentage of air pollution in various parts of the world?
questions.explanation: Automobiles are responsible for 60 percent of air pollution in various parts of the world.

questions.question: Which gas do automobiles release maximum amount of into the atmosphere?
questions.explanation: They release maximum carbon monoxide into the atmosphere.

questions.question: What might we have to wear on our noses in the future if pollution continues to increase?
questions.explanation: If this trend continues, we may have to wear nasal filters on our nose in future.

questions.question: What happens to rubber tyres on automobiles because of air pollution?
questions.explanation: Air pollution causes rubber tyres on automobiles to crack and become porous.

questions.question: Fine buildings become shabby because their walls are blackened with ________.
questions.explanation: Fine buildings become shabby, their walls blackened with soot that has settled on them.

questions.question: Periods of high levels of air pollution were linked to an increased number of deaths in which regions?
questions.explanation: In both the United States and Europe, high levels of air pollution were linked to increased deaths.

questions.question: Which of these gases is NOT mentioned as alarmingly increasing and causing the atmosphere to become warmer?
questions.explanation: The text lists carbon dioxide, methane, and nitrous oxide.

questions.question: The process where increasing gases trap radiation and make the atmosphere warmer is called ________.
questions.explanation: This process would eventually lead to global warming.

questions.question: CFCs were once widely used in which of the following?
questions.explanation: Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) were once widely used in spray cans.

questions.question: Acid rain contains precipitation with oxides of ________.
questions.explanation: Acid rain contains oxides of sulphur and nitrogen.

questions.question: In Sweden, how many lakes have been so affected by acid rain that no fish survived?
questions.explanation: In Sweden, 4000 lakes have been so severely affected that no fish has survived.

questions.question: Which of these is a nutrient that acid rain leaches away from the soil?
questions.explanation: It washes away nutrients like potassium, calcium and magnesium.

questions.question: What is left behind after acid rain kills large stretches of forests?
questions.explanation: Acid rain kills forests, leaving behind leafless skeletons of trees.

questions.question: Which bird in Sweden is threatened by acid rain?
questions.explanation: Among the species threatened is the Pied Flycatcher.

questions.question: From where has the Dipper fish vanished due to acid rain?
questions.explanation: The Dipper fish has vanished from the river of Central Wales.

questions.question: In which city is acid rain eating into the marble of world-famous monuments?
questions.explanation: In Athens, acid rain is eating into the marble of its world-famous monuments.

questions.question: According to experts, how much damage has been done in the past 25 years compared to the previous 2000?
questions.explanation: Experts say that more damage has been done in the past 25 years than in the previous 2000.

questions.question: Which approach to control air pollution involves raising the heights of smokestacks?
questions.explanation: Dispersal measures include raising the heights of smokestacks.

questions.question: Designing equipment to trap pollutants before they escape is known as which approach?
questions.explanation: Collection measures include designing equipment to trap pollutants.

questions.question: Acid rain originating in the United States caused the death of lakes in which region?
questions.explanation: The death of lakes in eastern Canada has been caused by acid rain that originated in the United States.

questions.question: Acids produced in which countries caused damage in Sweden?
questions.explanation: Acids produced in Britain and France have caused damage in Sweden.

questions.question: What device is used in new cars to change pollutants into harmless substances?
questions.explanation: New cars have been equipped with devices such as the catalytic converter.

questions.question: Which of these professionals is NOT mentioned as being involved in research for air pollution control?
questions.explanation: The text mentions physicians, engineers, meteorologists, and botanists.

questions.question: Air pollution is referred to as a 'hidden _________'.
questions.explanation: Air pollution is a hidden menace and poses the greatest threat.

questions.question: What word in the glossary means 'unpleasant'?
questions.explanation: Glossary: obnoxious - unpleasant.

questions.question: What is the meaning of 'spew' as used in the industrial context?
questions.explanation: Glossary: spew - throw out.

questions.question: What are 'smokestacks'?

options.B: Tall chimneys that carry smoke away from factories

questions.explanation: Glossary: smokestacks - tall chimneys that carry smoke away from factories.

questions.question: Which term describes a mixture of smoke and fog?
questions.explanation: Glossary: smog - a mixture of smoke and fog.

questions.question: What is the noun form of the verb 'respire'?
questions.explanation: The vocabulary section identifies 'respiration' as the noun form of 'respire'.

questions.question: The word 'smog' is formed by the process of ________.
questions.explanation: Two words have formed the word ‘smog’. Such process of word formation is known as blending.

questions.question: Which of these is a blended word for 'Foreign + exchange'?
questions.explanation: The exercise identifies Forex bank as Foreign + exchange bank.

questions.question: Which of these is a blended word for 'Slim + tender'?
questions.explanation: The exercise identifies 'Slender' as the blend for 'Slim + tender'.

questions.question: What is the blended word for 'Tele + broadcast'?
questions.explanation: The exercise identifies 'telecast' as Tele + broadcast.

questions.question: In the phrase 'irritating gases', what is the grammatical role of 'irritating'?
questions.explanation: The language section identifies 'irritating' as a present participle adjective.

questions.question: In the phrase 'polluted air', what is 'polluted'?
questions.explanation: The language section identifies 'polluted' as a past participle adjective.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'Air pollution causes ________ problem.'
questions.explanation: Using the present participle as an adjective: breathing problem.

questions.question: Which country's Clean Air Act was amended in 1990?
questions.explanation: The Clean Air Act of 1970 was amended in 1990 in the United States.

questions.question: The Federal Environment Protection Agency belongs to which country?
questions.explanation: Under this law [US Clean Air Act], the federal environment protection agency sets standards.

questions.question: Which city is mentioned as highly polluted and located in Greece?
questions.explanation: In Athens, a city which is highly polluted... [Athens is the capital of Greece].

questions.question: What is the meaning of 'leaches away'?
questions.explanation: Glossary: leaches away - washes away.

questions.question: The term 'lesions' refers to ________.
questions.explanation: Glossary: lesions - wounds or injuries.

questions.question: A person who studies weather conditions is a ________.
questions.explanation: Glossary: meteorologists - persons who study weather conditions.

questions.question: What is the meaning of 'menace' in the context of the poem?
questions.explanation: Glossary: menace - threat.

questions.explanation: Based on the vocabulary exercise patterns.

questions.question: What is the verb form of 'pollution'?
questions.explanation: Based on the vocabulary table in the text.

questions.question: The word 'industrial' is related to ________.
questions.explanation: Glossary: industrial - relating to industry.

questions.question: What describes air that has the wrong composition or irritating gases?
questions.explanation: If the composition is altered... the air is said to be polluted.

questions.question: Cattle have been poisoned by fumes from ________.
questions.explanation: Cattle have been poisoned by the fumes from smelters.

questions.question: Building surfaces may ________ because of air pollution.
questions.explanation: Building surfaces may actually deteriorate because of air pollution.

questions.question: According to the text, what contains oxides of sulphur and nitrogen?
questions.explanation: Acid rain... contains oxides of sulphur and nitrogen.

questions.question: The Brown Trout has vanished from lakes in which country?
questions.explanation: The Dipper fish has vanished... and the Brown Trout from Norwegian lakes.

questions.question: What is the noun form of 'alter'?
questions.explanation: Based on the table of word forms.

questions.question: What is the verb form of 'emission'?
questions.explanation: Based on the table of word forms.

questions.question: What happened to the Dipper fish?

options.B: It vanished from rivers in Central Wales.

questions.explanation: The Dipper fish has vanished from the river of Central Wales.

questions.question: Pollution control often leads to ________ for consumers.
questions.explanation: Often pollution control means higher prices.

questions.question: Which of these is a collection measure?
questions.explanation: Collection measures, such as designing equipment to trap pollutants.

questions.question: What is the noun form of 'illustrate'?
questions.explanation: Based on the word form table.

questions.question: According to the lead-in, air pollution is a threat to ________.
questions.explanation: Air pollution... poses the greatest threat to mankind in the future.
